record.model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M, both shards (native, not the requant)
record.expert_cache: 2.3 GB: the MTP head's 512 experts are resident in Q2_0 (675 MiB) and come out of this budget, so the main layers give up 0.7 GB of cache (M10 measured main-cache size 1 -> 3 GB as TPOT-neutral at chat, so this is the cheap end of the trade)
record.speculation: MTP --mtp-n-predict 4, one round trip per layer per step instead of per token (M16). MISTRALRS_MTP_PREFIX_REPLAY=none lifts the builtin-MTP Full replay, which otherwise kills both the snapshot and the restore; equivalence gated in M16 item 2
record.prefix_reuse: --prefix-cache-n 1 (one recurrent snapshot, ~111 MB), checkpoint at align_down(prompt, 32) since M16 item 1
record.prefill_chunking: --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-chunk-tokens 8192 are *ceilings*: the prefill path plans the step at warmup from the free VRAM it measures (chunk, and 1 or 2 layer buffers, from 160 MiB + 680 MiB per 1024 tokens of activations, Strata's formula, with an eighth of slack) and publishes it to the scheduler. On this card it lands on 1024 with one buffer
record.max_seqs: 4: the hybrid model reserves a ~112 MiB recurrent state per sequence slot, so the default 32 cost 3.5 GiB of VRAM for slots a one-request-at-a-time server never uses. At 4 the same card affords a 3 GB expert cache instead of 1 GB
record.drafter: MTP head's experts resident on the GPU in Q2_0 (moe::resident): 675 MiB, 2.25 bit/weight, same format/size strata uses; prefill 1696 rows 2.73 s -> 10.4 ms, draft forward 1.0-2.4 ms -> 0.55 ms
record.checkpoint_alignment: MISTRALRS_ALIGN_CHECKPOINTS=1 stops a verify step on the next paged block boundary, so the recurrent prefix checkpoint is taken at the end of every turn instead of only when a step happens to land on a boundary (measured 3/4 turns before). Costs nothing measurable: the dropped drafts are re-proposed next step and the continuation token is still sampled
